mainTopic: Early שבת and מוצאי שבת prayers, whether תפלת ערבית is רשות or חובה, and the removal of רבן גמליאל
overview: The גמרא first explains why רבי ירמיה בר אבא could daven behind רב, even though doing so is normally a serious disrespect: he was a תלמיד חבר. That story leads to a question: if someone davens the שבת תפילה early, must he stop doing מלאכה? The גמרא works through cases of a mistaken early תפילה, including a ציבור that davened מוצאי שבת too early. It then rules that one may daven שבת early and say קידוש, and may daven מוצאי שבת on שבת and say הבדלה. Next the גמרא explains the משנה's words that the evening prayer is 'not fixed': they follow the view that תפלת ערבית is רשות. רבן גמליאל says it is חובה, and רבי יהושע says it is רשות. A student's question brings this dispute into public, and רבן גמליאל leaves רבי יהושע standing in humiliation. The people decide to remove רבן גמליאל and choose רבי אלעזר בן עזריה in his place. He goes to consult his wife, and her answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The rule against davening next to or behind one's teacher
steps.stepSummary: This is the end of the challenge to רבי ירמיה בר אבא, who davened behind רב. One may not daven right beside his רב or behind him.
steps.simpleTranslation: [One may not pray] directly next to his teacher, and not behind his teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a rule that a student may not daven right beside his רב or behind him. It uses this rule to challenge the story that רבי ירמיה בר אבא davened behind רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Standing right beside your רב looks like you think you are his equal. Standing behind him looks like you are bowing to him. רבי ירמיה בר אבא did exactly the second thing, so his conduct seems to break the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Directly next to (level with) his teacher

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the END of a sentence that started on the previous amud. It is part of the challenge against רבי ירמיה בר אבא. It is not a new, separate teaching.

phrases.english: not directly next to his teacher,
phrases.notes: Continues a prohibition quoted on the previous amud.

phrases.english: and not behind his teacher.
phrases.notes: This is the part that clashes with רבי ירמיה בר אבא's behavior.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא כְּנֶגֶד רַבּוֹ, וְלֹא אֲחוֹרֵי רַבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge begun on the previous amud against רבי ירמיה בר אבא davening behind רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that רבי ירמיה בר אבא davened behind רב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known rule forbids davening behind one's רב, so a great אמורא should not have done it.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's harsher list of disrespect to a teacher
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא makes the challenge stronger. רבי אליעזר lists five acts of disrespect to one's רב, including davening behind him, that cause the שכינה to leave ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says: One who prays behind his teacher, one who greets his teacher first, one who returns his teacher's greeting [like an equal], one who sets up a rival ישיבה to his teacher's, and one who says something he did not hear from his teacher's mouth, causes the שכינה to leave ישראל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that makes the challenge even sharper. Davening behind your רב is listed with other acts of disrespect that drive the שכינה away from ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, davening behind your רב was simply forbidden. Now we learn it is serious enough to cause the שכינה to leave. That makes it much harder to explain how רבי ירמיה בר אבא could have done it.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was taught (in a ברייתא), bringing extra support
One who greets first (instead of waiting for his רב to greet him)
One who sets up a rival yeshiva against his רב's
That it should leave or withdraw

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is a main source for the laws of כבוד רבו, the honor a student owes his teacher.

phrases.english: And it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
phrases.notes: A ברייתא that strengthens the challenge.

phrases.english: One who prays behind his teacher,
phrases.notes: This is exactly what רבי ירמיה בר אבא did.

phrases.english: and one who greets his teacher,

phrases.english: and one who returns his teacher's greeting,
phrases.notes: Meaning he answers like an equal, without saying 'Greetings to you, my teacher.'

phrases.english: and one who opposes his teacher's yeshiva,
phrases.notes: Opening his own yeshiva without his רב's permission.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאוֹמֵר דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא שָׁמַע מִפִּי רַבּוֹ —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a stronger source to the same challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה בר אבא davening behind רב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If this act drives away the שכינה, it cannot be allowed. So how did רבי ירמיה בר אבא do it?

steps.title: רבי ירמיה בר אבא was a תלמיד חבר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי ירמיה בר אבא was a תלמיד חבר, a student who is also a colleague, so these rules did not apply to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה בר אבא is different, because he was a student-colleague (תלמיד חבר).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבי ירמיה בר אבא was not an ordinary student of רב. He was a תלמיד חבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules of honor in steps 1 and 2 apply to a regular student. A תלמיד חבר is close to his teacher's level, so davening behind רב was allowed for him. The rule itself stays in place. Only this special type of person is an exception.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different (introduces an answer that sets this case apart)
A student who is also a colleague of his teacher

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the halachic category of תלמיד חבר, which matters for many laws of honoring a רב.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba is different
phrases.notes: Sets his case apart from the general rule.

phrases.english: because he was a student-colleague.
phrases.notes: The reason the rules did not apply to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 1 and 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the person: the rule is for a regular student, and this was a תלמיד חבר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed רבי ירמיה בר אבא was a regular student of רב and broke the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: As a תלמיד חבר, he was allowed to daven behind רב.

steps.title: Proof from how רבי ירמיה spoke to רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that רבי ירמיה בר אבא was a colleague. He asked רב 'Did you stop?' and not 'Did the Master stop?'
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is why רבי ירמיה בר אבא said to רב: Did you separate [from work]? He said to him: Yes, I separated. And he did not say, 'Did the Master (מר) separate?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the answer. When רב davened the שבת תפילה early, רבי ירמיה בר אבא asked him in plain 'you' language, like an equal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular student would say 'Did the Master...' (מר) out of respect. Because רבי ירמיה בר אבא said 'you,' this shows he was a תלמיד חבר. The story also raises a new topic: after davening שבת early, must a person stop doing מלאכה?

keyTerms.meaning: And this is why (brings support for what was just said)
Did you separate yourself (from מלאכה, accepting שבת)?
The Master (a respectful way to address a רב)

steps.confusionAlert: 'מי בדלת' does not mean 'Who separated?' Here מי is a question word meaning 'Did...?' The question is whether רב stopped doing מלאכה after davening the שבת תפילה early.

phrases.english: And this is why he said to him
phrases.notes: Brings a story to support the תלמיד חבר answer.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba to Rav:
phrases.notes: Background: רב had davened the שבת תפילה before nightfall.

phrases.english: Did you separate yourself?
phrases.notes: Meaning: did you stop doing מלאכה and accept שבת?

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes, I separated myself,
phrases.notes: רב's answer.

phrases.english: and he did not say, 'Did the Master separate?'
phrases.notes: The proof: he spoke to רב as an equal.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּקָאָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא לְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי ירמיה בר אבא was a תלמיד חבר of רב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: He addressed רב with 'you' and not with the respectful 'מר.'

steps.title: Must one really stop work after davening שבת early?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רב truly had to stop מלאכה after davening early. רבי davened the שבת תפילה before dark and then went to the bathhouse.
steps.simpleTranslation: But did he need to separate? Didn't רבי אבין say: Once רבי prayed the שבת prayer on Friday afternoon, went into the bathhouse, came out and taught us our chapters, and it was still not dark!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new question raised by the story. It challenges the idea that davening שבת early forces a person to stop מלאכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said he stopped מלאכה after davening early. But רבי davened the שבת תפילה and then went to the bathhouse while it was still day. That suggests early davening does not make you accept שבת's restrictions.

keyTerms.meaning: But does he (really have to) separate?

phrases.english: But does he separate?
phrases.notes: Questions what רב said he did.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Avin say:
phrases.notes: Brings a source against it.

phrases.english: Once Rabbi prayed
phrases.notes: רבי means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: the Shabbat prayer on Shabbat eve,
phrases.notes: He davened early, before nightfall.

phrases.english: and entered the bathhouse,
phrases.notes: Apparently not acting as if שבת had started.

phrases.english: and came out and taught us our chapters,
and it had not yet become dark!
phrases.notes: All of this happened while it was still day.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי בְּדֵיל? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up a detail from the proof story in step 4 and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that he separated from מלאכה after davening the שבת תפילה early.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי went to the bathhouse after davening early, which suggests no need to separate.

steps.title: רבא: he only went in to sweat, before the גזירה
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that רבי went into the bathhouse only to sweat. This was before חכמים made a גזירה against sweating on שבת, so it was allowed even on שבת itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: That was a case where he entered to sweat, and it was before the decree (גזירה).
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge. What רבי did would have been allowed even on שבת at that time, so the story proves nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sweating in a bathhouse is not a מלאכה, and in רבי's time it was not yet forbidden by a גזירה. So רבי may have accepted שבת when he davened and still done nothing wrong. The idea that early davening means stopping מלאכה still stands.
steps.whatToRemember: A regular student may not daven behind or right beside his רב, but a תלמיד חבר may. Davening the שבת תפילה early can mean accepting שבת and stopping מלאכה. רבי's bathhouse visit does not disprove this, because sweating was allowed before the גזירה.

phrases.english: Rava said:
That was where he entered to sweat,
phrases.notes: Not to wash, only to sweat.

phrases.english: and it was before the decree.
phrases.notes: Later חכמים forbade sweating in a bathhouse on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הָהוּא דְּנִכְנַס לְהַזִּיעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the act was allowed even on שבת at that time.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי's bathhouse visit showed he had not accepted שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sweating before the גזירה was allowed on שבת, so there is no proof against stopping מלאכה after davening early.

steps.title: Permission to work after praying early
steps.stepSummary: אביי permitted רב דימי בר ליואי to fumigate baskets after he had prayed the שבת תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? Didn’t אביי permit רב דימי בר ליואי to fumigate baskets?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a case that seems to challenge the idea that praying the שבת תפילה early requires a person to stop working.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fumigating baskets is work. If רב דימי בר ליואי had already prayed the שבת תפילה, why did אביי allow him to do it?

phrases.english: Is that so? Didn’t Abaye permit him

phrases.aramaic: לְרַב דִּימִי בַּר לֵיוַאי לְכַבְרוֹיֵי סַלֵּי!
phrases.english: Rav Dimi bar Liva’ei, to fumigate baskets!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי, וְהָא אַבָּיֵי שְׁרָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the previous answer explained why רבי could enter the bathhouse, this case raises a new challenge about doing work after an early שבת תפילה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that praying the שבת תפילה early prevents further work.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי allowed work in a case where the person had already prayed.

steps.title: That prayer happened by mistake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב דימי בר ליואי prayed because of a mistake, not because he meant to begin שבת early.
steps.simpleTranslation: That was a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא distinguishes this case from someone who deliberately prays the שבת תפילה early.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי בר ליואי did not intend to begin שבת early. The answer says that his mistaken prayer did not require him to stop working.

phrases.english: That was a mistake.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא טָעוּתָא הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why אביי could permit work in the case just raised.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes a mistaken early prayer from an intentional one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any early שבת תפילה requires the person to stop working.
steps.terutzMaskana: This mistaken תפילה does not have that consequence.

steps.title: A mistaken prayer that still stood
steps.stepSummary: A story about a ציבור seems to show that a mistaken תפילה is not simply undone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can a mistake be reversed? Didn’t אבידן say: Once clouds covered the sky, and the people thought it was dark. They entered the בית הכנסת and prayed the מוצאי שבת prayer while it was still שבת. The clouds cleared and the sun shone. They asked רבי, who said: Since they prayed, they prayed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer by telling a story in which a mistaken תפילה was left standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ציבור prayed for מוצאי שבת while it was still שבת, yet רבי said their prayer stood. That seems to challenge the claim that a mistaken תפילה can be treated as though it did not change anything.
steps.confusionAlert: The story is about mistakenly praying for מוצאי שבת before שבת ended; the earlier case was about mistakenly praying the שבת תפילה early. The גמרא compares what happens to a mistaken תפילה, not two identical prayers.

Didn’t Avidan say: Once,
the sky filled with clouds, and the people thought

phrases.english: that it was dark; they entered the synagogue
and prayed the prayer for the end of Shabbat while it was still Shabbat.
The clouds cleared, and the sun shone,
and they came and asked Rabbi.
And he said: Since they prayed, they prayed!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְטָעוּתָא מִי הָדְרָא? וְהָא אָמַר אֲבִידָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim that the mistaken early תפילה has no effect on what the person may do afterward.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that treats רב דימי בר ליואי’s mistaken תפילה differently from an intentional early תפילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי allowed the ציבור’s mistaken תפילה to stand, suggesting that a mistaken תפילה is not simply reversible.

steps.title: A community is treated differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits רבי’s ruling to a ציבור, whom we do not burden with praying again.
steps.simpleTranslation: A community is different, because we do not burden them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the story about the ציבור does not establish the rule for an individual.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי left the ציבור’s mistaken prayer in place to avoid making everyone pray again. That special reason does not settle what follows from רב דימי בר ליואי’s mistaken תפילה.
steps.whatToRemember: The ציבור’s mistaken תפילה stood because requiring everyone to pray again would burden them. It therefore does not overturn the answer about the individual’s mistaken שבת תפילה.

phrases.english: A community is different, because we do not burden them.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי צִבּוּר, דְּלָא מַטְרְחִינַן לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits what can be learned from the story about רבי and the ציבור.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes a community from an individual.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because רבי left the ציבור’s mistaken תפילה standing, every mistaken תפילה must have the same result.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ציבור’s result reflects the special concern not to burden a community.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ציבור’s case does not refute the answer that רב דימי בר ליואי was permitted to work after his mistaken תפילה.

steps.title: Two examples of early evening prayer
steps.stepSummary: רב prayed the שבת prayer before שבת, and רבי יאשיה prayed the מוצאי שבת prayer while it was still שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבין said: רב prayed the שבת prayer on ערב שבת; רבי יאשיה prayed the מוצאי שבת prayer on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא introduces two examples of praying an evening prayer early. These examples set up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first prayer looks ahead to שבת. The second looks ahead to מוצאי שבת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Avin said:

phrases.aramaic: רַב צַלִּי שֶׁל שַׁבָּת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: Rav prayed the Shabbat prayer on Friday,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה מְצַלֵּי שֶׁל מוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoshiya would pray the post-Shabbat prayer on Shabbat.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The statement reports two instances of early prayer; it does not yet address prayer over a cup.

steps.title: Can early שבת prayer be followed by קידוש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רב also said קידוש over a cup before שבת began.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב prayed the שבת prayer on Friday, did he say the sanctification over a cup, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the first example and asks a new question about it. The question is about the cup, not about whether רב prayed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that רב prayed early. We do not yet know whether the early prayer allowed him to say קידוש over a cup at that time.

keyTerms.meaning: The cup used for the recitation

phrases.aramaic: רַב צַלִּי שֶׁל שַׁבָּת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת:

Does he recite sanctification over the cup,

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether one may say קידוש over a cup after praying the שבת prayer early.

steps.title: A teaching permits early קידוש
steps.stepSummary: A teaching from שמואל says that one may pray the שבת prayer early and say קידוש over a cup.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב נחמן said that שמואל said a person may pray the שבת prayer on Friday and recite sanctification over the cup.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that answers the question. It explicitly permits both the early prayer and קידוש over a cup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof supplies the detail missing from the report about רב. It gives a rule rather than claiming to know exactly what רב did afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear; an invitation to consider a source

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:

and recite sanctification over the cup.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the question about קידוש with an explicit teaching.
steps.raayaObject: קידוש over a cup may follow an early שבת prayer.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of שמואל transmitted by רב נחמן.

steps.title: The ruling follows that teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules like the teaching that permits early קידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the law is in accordance with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states its ruling for the early שבת prayer and קידוש question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous teaching did more than offer a possible answer. The גמרא now adopts its rule.
steps.whatToRemember: One may pray the שבת prayer early on ערב שבת and say קידוש over a cup.

phrases.english: And the law is in accordance with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It adopts the rule just cited.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ruling permits קידוש over a cup after the early שבת prayer.

steps.title: Can early מוצאי שבת prayer be followed by הבדלה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יאשיה said הבדלה over a cup while it was still שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי יאשיה prayed the מוצאי שבת prayer on שבת, did he recite הבדלה over the cup, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the second early-prayer example. It asks whether הבדלה over a cup can also be said early.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ruling concerned the start of שבת and קידוש. This question concerns the end of שבת and הבדלה, so it needs its own answer.

keyTerms.meaning: The recitation marking separation from Shabbat

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה מְצַלֵּי שֶׁל מוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת בְּשַׁבָּת:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoshiya would pray the post-Shabbat prayer on Shabbat:
Does he recite separation over the cup

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אוֹמֵר הַבְדָּלָה עַל הַכּוֹס?
phrases.english: or does he not recite separation over the cup?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה מְצַלֵּי שֶׁל מוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת בְּשַׁבָּת:
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It asks the parallel question about the other end of שבת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether הבדלה over a cup may follow a מוצאי שבת prayer said while it is still שבת.

steps.title: A teaching permits early הבדלה
steps.stepSummary: A teaching from שמואל permits both the early מוצאי שבת prayer and הבדלה over a cup.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב יהודה said that שמואל said a person may pray the מוצאי שבת prayer on שבת and recite הבדלה over the cup.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an explicit teaching to answer the הבדלה question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As with קידוש, the source gives a general rule. It does not depend on knowing what רבי יאשיה personally did after praying.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: מִתְפַּלֵּל אָדָם שֶׁל מוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת בְּשַׁבָּת
phrases.english: A person may pray the post-Shabbat prayer on Shabbat
and recite separation over the cup.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It supplies the requested rule for הבדלה.
steps.raayaObject: הבדלה over a cup may follow an early מוצאי שבת prayer.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of שמואל transmitted by רב יהודה.

steps.title: A reported example beside a pillar
steps.stepSummary: A chain of sages reports that רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי prayed the שבת prayer early beside a particular pillar.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said that רבי אסי said that רבי אלעזר said that רבי חנינא said that רב said: Beside this pillar, רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוסי prayed the שבת prayer on Friday.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a specific story of early prayer. It identifies the person, the place, and which prayer he said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is another reported example, not a new question about a cup. All three details will matter because the next speaker gives a different version.

keyTerms.meaning: The first named transmitter of this report
The person named in this version of the story

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rabbi Asi said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Elazar said that Rabbi Ḥanina said that Rav said:
Beside this pillar prayed
Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yosei,
the Shabbat prayer on Friday

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר רַב:
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the rule about הבדלה, the גמרא supplies a further story about early prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: This version reports an early שבת prayer by רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי beside a pillar.

steps.title: A different version of the story
steps.stepSummary: עולא corrects the reported place, person, and prayer: a palm tree, רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי, and a מוצאי שבת prayer said on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: When עולא came, he said: It was beside a palm tree, not a pillar. It was רבי אלעזר son of רבי יוסי, not רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוסי. And it was the מוצאי שבת prayer on שבת, not the שבת prayer on Friday.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives a different account of the same story. He changes three concrete details.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prayer in עולא’s version is an early מוצאי שבת prayer. His correction challenges the previous version of the story, not the earlier teachings about קידוש and הבדלה over a cup.

keyTerms.meaning: The sage who gives the differing version
The person named in עולא’s version

steps.whatToRemember: עולא changes the place, the person, and the prayer—not the earlier rule about the cup.

phrases.english: When Ulla came, he said:
It was beside a palm tree,
and it was not beside a pillar.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הֲוָה,
phrases.english: And it was not Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הֲוָה,
phrases.english: but Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Yosei.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא שֶׁל שַׁבָּת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת הֲוָה,
phrases.english: And it was not the Shabbat prayer on Friday,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁל מוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת בְּשַׁבָּת הֲוָה.
phrases.english: but the post-Shabbat prayer on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא עוּלָּא אָמַר:
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It replaces three details in the account just reported.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The place, person, and type of early prayer in the preceding story.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: According to עולא’s account, the preceding report has all three details wrong.

steps.title: What does “not fixed” mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words about the evening prayer (תפלת הערב אין לה קבע) and asks what they mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] The evening prayer is not fixed. What does “is not fixed” mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה's words about the evening prayer and asks what exactly is 'not fixed.' This sets up the next steps, which test two possible meanings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words could be about the prayer’s time or about whether one must pray it. The question sets up a choice between those meanings.

phrases.english: The evening prayer is not fixed.
What does “is not fixed” mean?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אֵין לָהּ קֶבַע?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does אֵין לָהּ קֶבַע say about the evening prayer?

steps.title: Why not simply say “all night”?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests a time-based reading and challenges the wording it would require.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it means that one may pray whenever one wishes throughout the night, let it say, “The evening prayer is all night”!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the idea that the statement only describes how late one may pray. It objects that this could have been said much more directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the point were just the time limit, “all night” would express it plainly. That makes the גמרא look for a different meaning of “not fixed.”

phrases.english: If you say that, if one wishes, one may pray
throughout the whole night,
let it teach: “The evening prayer is all night”!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא דְּאִי בָּעֵי מְצַלֵּי כּוּלֵּיהּ לֵילְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and challenges one possible answer to the wording question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that אֵין לָהּ קֶבַע only means one may pray all night.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that were the intended point, the statement could simply say כׇּל הַלַּיְלָה.

steps.title: The wording points to an optional prayer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the wording question and offers a different reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does “is not fixed” mean? It follows the one who says that the evening prayer is optional.
steps.whatsHappening: The opening question sets up the next answer: “not fixed” is about the prayer’s status, not just its time. The answer connects the wording to the view that the evening prayer is optional.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rejected reading concerned when the prayer may be said. This reading concerns whether praying it is required.

keyTerms.meaning: in accordance with the one who says

phrases.english: Rather, what does “is not fixed” mean—
It follows the one who says: The evening prayer is optional.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי אֵין לָהּ קֶבַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the challenged time-based reading with a reading about obligation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A different interpretation of the wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אֵין לָהּ קֶבַע describes a prayer that may be said all night.
steps.terutzMaskana: Here it is read in line with the view that תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית is רְשׁוּת.

steps.title: Two views on the evening prayer
steps.stepSummary: A report from רב יהודה in the name of שמואל identifies who calls the prayer obligatory and who calls it optional.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: Regarding the evening prayer, רבן גמליאל says it is obligatory, and רבי יהושע says it is optional.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the disagreement behind the previous answer. רבן גמליאל says the prayer is required; רבי יהושע says it is optional.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous step referred to “the one who says” it is optional. This report identifies that view as רבי יהושע’s and gives the opposing view of רבן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage in whose name it is reported
the sage who says the prayer is obligatory
the sage who says the prayer is optional

phrases.english: For Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:

phrases.aramaic: תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר חוֹבָה,
phrases.english: The evening prayer: Rabban Gamliel says it is obligatory,
and Rabbi Yehoshua says it is optional.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the two sides of the disagreement mentioned in the answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל calls תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית חוֹבָה; רבי יהושע calls it רְשׁוּת.

steps.title: אביי and רבא disagree about the ruling
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules like the obligatory view, while רבא rules like the optional view.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The law follows the one who says it is obligatory. And רבא said: The law follows the one who says it is optional.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives two opposing rulings about the disagreement. It does not settle their disagreement here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי sides with רבן גמליאל’s view. רבא sides with רבי יהושע’s view.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage who rules for the obligatory view
the law follows the words of
the sage who rules for the optional view

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי הָאוֹמֵר חוֹבָה.
phrases.english: Abaye said: The law follows the one who says it is obligatory.

phrases.aramaic: וְרָבָא אָמַר: הֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי הָאוֹמֵר רְשׁוּת.
phrases.english: And Rava said: The law follows the one who says it is optional.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי הָאוֹמֵר חוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from identifying the two views to reporting opposing rulings about them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי rules like the חוֹבָה view; רבא rules like the רְשׁוּת view.

steps.title: A student receives opposite answers
steps.stepSummary: An account shows a student asking רבי יהושע and רבן גמליאל the same question and receiving different answers.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sages taught: A student came before רבי יהושע and asked whether the evening prayer is optional or obligatory. He answered, “Optional.” The student came before רבן גמליאל and asked the same question. He answered, “Obligatory.”
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins an account that puts the disagreement into a conversation. One student hears “optional” from רבי יהושע and “obligatory” from רבן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two answers match the views just reported. The student has now heard a direct contradiction, which sets up his next question.

phrases.english: The sages taught: There was an incident involving a student
who came before Rabbi Yehoshua.
He asked him: Is the evening prayer
optional or obligatory?
He answered him: Optional.
He came before Rabban Gamliel,
and asked him: Is the evening prayer
optional or obligatory?
He answered him: Obligatory.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּתַלְמִיד אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins an account of the disagreement after the opposing rulings were reported.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the account, רבי יהושע answers רְשׁוּת and רבן גמליאל answers חוֹבָה.

steps.title: The student points out the conflicting answer
steps.stepSummary: The student challenges רבן גמליאל’s answer by reporting what רבי יהושע told him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But didn’t רבי יהושע tell me it is optional?!
steps.whatsHappening: The student tells רבן גמליאל that רבי יהושע gave the opposite answer. He asks how the two answers can stand together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a new legal view. It is a challenge based on the answer the student personally received.

keyTerms.meaning: optional or obligatory—the choice behind the conflicting answers

phrases.english: He said to him: But didn’t Rabbi Yehoshua
tell me it is optional?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: וַהֲלֹא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר לִי רְשׁוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second answer by comparing it with the first.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן גמליאל’s answer that תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית is חוֹבָה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהושע told the same student that it is רְשׁוּת.

steps.title: The discussion is deferred until the scholars arrive
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל tells the student to wait for the scholars to enter the study hall.
steps.simpleTranslation: He told him: Wait until the masters of the shields enter the study hall.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל does not resolve the disagreement yet. He tells the student to wait until the scholars enter the study hall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer changes the setting for the discussion rather than answering the legal question. It prepares the next part of the account.

keyTerms.meaning: literally “masters of shields”; here, scholars who debate

phrases.english: He told him: Wait until they enter—
the masters of the shields—into the study hall.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: הַמְתֵּן עַד שֶׁיִּכָּנְסוּ בַּעֲלֵי תְּרִיסִין לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the student’s challenge by postponing the discussion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Wait for the scholars to enter; no ruling resolving the contradiction is given yet.

steps.title: The Student Asks His Question in Public
steps.stepSummary: Once the scholars enter the בית המדרש, the student stands up and publicly asks whether תפלת ערבית is רשות or חובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the scholars (the 'shield-bearers') came in, the questioner stood up and asked: Is the evening prayer optional or obligatory?
steps.whatsHappening: This is what רבן גמליאל was waiting for in the last step. The scholars are now present, so the student repeats his question in front of everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question itself is the same one from before. What is new is the setting: it is now asked in public, in front of all the חכמים. This sets up a public test of who holds which view.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Masters of the shields', a name for the great scholars who 'battle' in Torah debate
The questioner, meaning the student from the earlier steps

phrases.english: When the masters of the shields entered,
the questioner stood and asked:
Is the evening prayer optional or obligatory?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁנִּכְנְסוּ בַּעֲלֵי תְּרִיסִין, עָמַד הַשּׁוֹאֵל וְשָׁאַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out רבן גמליאל's instruction to wait until the scholars enter.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether תפלת ערבית is רשות or חובה, asked publicly before the חכמים.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל Answers: חובה
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל publicly answers that תפלת ערבית is חובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said to him: It is obligatory.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל gives the same answer he gave in private: the evening prayer is required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing has changed in his ruling. Now it is said in front of everyone, which makes it an official public position.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel said to him: Obligatory.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: חוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the public question of step 27.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל Asks If Anyone Disagrees
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל asks the חכמים whether anyone disputes his ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said to the חכמים: Is there anyone who disagrees about this?
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל turns to the scholars and checks whether anyone holds a different view. This sets up the next move, where רבי יהושע will be tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל already knows the student heard רשות from רבי יהושע. His question invites רבי יהושע to either stand by his view in public or back down.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there at all...? (a question word)

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel said to the Sages:

phrases.aramaic: כְּלוּם יֵשׁ אָדָם שֶׁחוֹלֵק בְּדָבָר זֶה?
phrases.english: Is there any person who disputes this matter?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלוּם יֵשׁ אָדָם שֶׁחוֹלֵק בְּדָבָר זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ruling, רבן גמליאל checks for public disagreement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether any חכם openly disputes the ruling of חובה.

steps.title: רבי יהושע Says No
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע answers that no one disagrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: No.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע does not argue in public. He says that no one disputes the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Out of respect for the נשיא, רבי יהושע chooses not to argue openly. This creates a gap between what he told the student privately and what he says now, and the next step attacks that gap.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: No.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: לָאו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבן גמליאל's question about disagreement.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No one disputes the ruling of חובה.

steps.title: But They Quoted You as Saying Optional
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל challenges רבי יהושע: wasn't the ruling of רשות reported to him in רבי יהושע's name?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But didn't they tell me in your name that it is optional?
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל confronts רבי יהושע. He points out that the student reported רבי יהושע's ruling of רשות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע just said no one disagrees, but רבן גמליאל has a report that he does. The challenge exposes the contradiction in front of everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that...? (a challenging question)

steps.confusionAlert: Here it is רבן גמליאל who speaks, quoting what the student told him. The student himself is not the speaker in this line.

phrases.english: He said to him: But was it not in your name
that they told me: optional!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא מִשִּׁמְךָ אָמְרוּ לִי רְשׁוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יהושע's denial in step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's claim that no one disagrees
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ruling of רשות was reported in his own name, so he himself disagrees.

steps.title: Stand Up and Let Them Testify
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל orders רבי יהושע to stand while witnesses confirm what he said.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: יהושע, stand on your feet, and they will testify against you.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל tells רבי יהושע to stand up so the witnesses can confirm the report. This sets up רבי יהושע's response.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Standing while witnesses testify is like a person on trial. The scene moves from a halachic question to a public embarrassment of רבי יהושע.

keyTerms.meaning: And they will testify against you

phrases.english: He said to him: Yehoshua,
stand on your feet and they will testify against you.

steps.triggerLanguage: יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, עֲמוֹד עַל רַגְלֶיךָ וְיָעִידוּ בְּךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the challenge of step 31 into a formal confrontation with witnesses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע must stand while witnesses confirm he ruled רשות.

steps.title: רבי יהושע Admits: The Living Cannot Deny the Living
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע stands and admits he said it, because the witness is alive and present.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע stood up and said: If I were alive and he were dead, the living could deny the dead. But now that I am alive and he is alive, how can the living deny the living?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע stands as ordered and admits that he did rule רשות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He explains that he could deny a report from someone who had died, since that person could not answer back. But the student is alive and standing here, so denial is impossible and he must admit it.

phrases.aramaic: עָמַד רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ עַל רַגְלָיו וְאָמַר
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua stood on his feet and said:
If I were alive and he were dead,
the living can contradict the dead.
But now that I am alive and he is alive,

phrases.aramaic: הֵיאַךְ יָכוֹל הַחַי לְהַכְחִישׁ אֶת הַחַי?
phrases.english: how can the living contradict the living?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִלְמָלֵא אֲנִי חַי וְהוּא מֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the challenge and the order to stand by admitting the ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהושע admits he ruled רשות, since he cannot deny a living witness.

steps.title: רבי יהושע Left Standing and the Crowd Stops the Lecture
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל keeps lecturing while רבי יהושע stands. The people grow upset and tell the speaker, חוצפית, to stop, and he stops.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל sat and lectured while רבי יהושע stood on his feet, until all the people murmured and said to חוצפית the speaker: Stop! And he stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל never tells רבי יהושע to sit down and simply goes on teaching. The crowd becomes angry and halts the lecture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving רבי יהושע standing is seen as a public humiliation. The people stop the התורגמן, the man who repeats the lecture aloud, which in effect shuts down רבן גמליאל's teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: The speaker who repeated the lecture aloud to the crowd
Here it means 'stop' (stand still and stop speaking)

steps.confusionAlert: The word עֲמוֹד said to חוצפית does not mean 'stand up' as it did for רבי יהושע. Here it means 'stop.'

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel was sitting and lecturing
and Rabbi Yehoshua was standing on his feet,
until all the people murmured
and said to Chutzpit the disseminator:
Stop! And he stopped.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל יוֹשֵׁב וְדוֹרֵשׁ וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ עוֹמֵד עַל רַגְלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes what happened after רבי יהושע's admission: he was left standing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The public humiliation of רבי יהושע leads the crowd to halt רבן גמליאל's lecture.

steps.title: This Is the Third Time He Hurt Him
steps.stepSummary: The people list earlier times רבן גמליאל pained רבי יהושע, on ראש השנה and in the case of בכורות with רבי צדוק, and now a third time.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: How long will he keep hurting him? Last year on ראש השנה he hurt him. In the matter of בכורות, in the case of רבי צדוק, he hurt him. Here too he hurts him.
steps.whatsHappening: The crowd builds a case against רבן גמליאל by showing this is a repeated pattern, not a one-time event. This sets up their decision in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is the pattern itself: three separate incidents. On ראש השנה he made רבי יהושע come with his staff and bag on the day that רבי יהושע counted as יום כיפור, and in בכורות he also left him standing. Repeated pain shows this is a real problem of leadership.

keyTerms.meaning: Will he pain him, cause him distress
Firstborn animals (the topic of the earlier dispute)

phrases.english: They said: How long will he continue afflicting him?
Last year on Rosh HaShanah he afflicted him.
Regarding firstborn animals, in the incident of Rabbi Tzadok, he afflicted him.
Here too he is afflicting him.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כַּמָּה נְצַעֲרֵיהּ וְנֵיזִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the crowd's anger from step 34 by pointing to past incidents.
steps.raayaObject: That רבן גמליאל repeatedly pains רבי יהושע
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ראש השנה incident, the בכורות incident with רבי צדוק, and the present incident

steps.title: Let Us Remove Him
steps.stepSummary: The people decide to remove רבן גמליאל from his position as נשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come, let us remove him!
steps.whatsHappening: Based on the repeated pattern, the people conclude that רבן גמליאל should be removed from leadership.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The halachic question about תפלת ערבית has turned into a question of leadership. This decision opens the next part of the story: deposing the נשיא and choosing a replacement.

keyTerms.meaning: And let us remove him (from office)

steps.whatToRemember: A disagreement over whether תפלת ערבית is רשות or חובה led to the public humiliation of רבי יהושע. Because רבן גמליאל had hurt him repeatedly, the people decided to remove רבן גמליאל as נשיא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the famous episode of רבן גמליאל's removal and the appointment of a new נשיא, which shapes the rest of the sugya on this daf.

phrases.english: Come, let us remove him!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא וְנַעְבְּרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical conclusion from the pattern listed in step 35.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The people resolve to depose רבן גמליאל from the נשיאות.

steps.title: Who will replace the leader?
steps.stepSummary: Having decided to remove רבן גמליאל, the חכמים ask whom they should appoint in his place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whom shall we appoint in his place?
steps.whatsHappening: The Sages have just agreed to remove רבן גמליאל, and now they face the practical question of who should replace him. This question sets up the next few steps, where candidates are suggested and judged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing a leader is only half the decision, because someone must step in. The question opens a short search, and each candidate will be checked against a specific concern.

phrases.english: Whom shall we appoint (in his place)?
phrases.notes: נוקים means to stand someone up, that is, to appoint him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן נוֹקֵים לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows directly from the decision to remove רבן גמליאל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is the right person to replace רבן גמליאל as נשיא?

steps.title: Not רבי יהושע, because he was part of the conflict
steps.stepSummary: The Sages consider רבי יהושע and reject him because he was the person directly involved in the incident.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we appoint רבי יהושע? No, because he was a party to the incident.
steps.whatsHappening: The first candidate suggested is רבי יהושע, and he is turned down. He was the one רבן גמליאל embarrassed, so giving him the job would look like personal revenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Appointing the injured party would deeply hurt רבן גמליאל and make the change look like a personal victory. The Sages want the change to be about leadership, not about one rabbi defeating another.

keyTerms.meaning: A party to the incident, someone directly involved

phrases.english: Shall we appoint Rabbi Yehoshua?
phrases.notes: The first candidate is suggested.

phrases.english: He is a party to the incident.
phrases.notes: This is the reason for rejecting him: it would be too painful for רבן גמליאל.

steps.triggerLanguage: נוֹקְמֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בַּעַל מַעֲשֶׂה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes and rejects the first candidate in answer to the question.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי יהושע as a candidate.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: He was personally involved in the dispute, so appointing him would be too painful and look personal.

steps.title: Not רבי עקיבא, because he lacks זכות אבות
steps.stepSummary: The Sages consider רבי עקיבא and reject him because he has no זכות אבות to protect him if רבן גמליאל's resentment brings punishment on him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we appoint רבי עקיבא? Perhaps רבן גמליאל will cause him to be punished, since he does not have ancestral merit.
steps.whatsHappening: The second candidate, רבי עקיבא, is also turned down. The worry is about his safety: he comes from a family of converts, so he has no ancestral merit to shield him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Sages fear that the hurt feelings of a great person like רבן גמליאל could bring divine punishment on whoever takes his place. Ancestral merit acts like a protective shield, and רבי עקיבא does not have one.

keyTerms.meaning: He will (cause him to) be punished

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a criticism of רבי עקיבא's greatness. The concern is only that he lacks the protection of זכות אבות.

phrases.english: Shall we appoint Rabbi Akiva?
phrases.notes: The second candidate is suggested.

phrases.english: Perhaps he (Rabban Gamliel) will cause him to be punished,
phrases.notes: The fear is divine punishment brought on by רבן גמליאל's resentment.

phrases.english: since he does not have ancestral merit.
phrases.notes: רבי עקיבא descended from converts.

steps.triggerLanguage: נוֹקְמֵיהּ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דִּילְמָא עָנֵישׁ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second candidate is proposed and rejected, for a different reason.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי עקיבא as a candidate.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: He lacks זכות אבות, so he would be exposed to punishment.

steps.title: The choice: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה
steps.stepSummary: The Sages choose רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, who is wise, rich, and a tenth-generation descendant of עזרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, let us appoint רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, for he is wise, he is rich, and he is the tenth generation from עזרא.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the first two candidates, the Sages land on רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. They list three qualities that make him the right fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא signals that the earlier options are set aside and this is the real answer. His three qualities will each be explained in the next step as answers to a specific need.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא נוֹקְמֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה,
phrases.english: Rather, let us appoint Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya,
phrases.notes: This is the final choice.

phrases.english: for he is wise, and he is rich,
phrases.notes: The first two qualities.

phrases.english: and he is the tenth generation from Ezra.
phrases.notes: The third quality: his distinguished lineage.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא נוֹקְמֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 37 after the rejections in steps 38 and 39.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה should be appointed, because he is wise, rich, and of distinguished lineage.

steps.title: Why each of his three qualities matters
steps.stepSummary: Each quality is explained. His wisdom lets him answer רבן גמליאל's challenges. His wealth lets him represent the community at the Caesar's court. His lineage gives him זכות אבות, so he cannot be punished.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is wise, so if (רבן גמליאל) challenges him, he can answer. He is rich, so if there is a need to serve at the Caesar's court, he too can go and serve. He is tenth from עזרא, so he has ancestral merit and (רבן גמליאל) cannot cause him to be punished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains why each of the three qualities makes רבי אלעזר בן עזריה suitable. Each quality answers a specific practical need or worry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wisdom means he will not be embarrassed in Torah debate with רבן גמליאל. Wealth lets him cover the costs of representing the Jewish people before the Roman government. His ancestry gives him exactly the protection that רבי עקיבא lacked, which solves the concern raised in step 39.

keyTerms.meaning: To serve or pay homage at the Caesar's court

steps.whatToRemember: The new leader was chosen to fill three needs: Torah strength, the means to represent the community before the government, and spiritual protection through זכות אבות.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא חָכָם — דְּאִי מַקְשֵׁי לֵיהּ, מְפָרֵק לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: He is wise, so if he (Rabban Gamliel) challenges him, he will answer it.
phrases.notes: His wisdom protects him from embarrassment in debate.

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא עָשִׁיר — דְּאִי אִית לֵיהּ לְפַלּוֹחֵי לְבֵי קֵיסָר,
phrases.english: And he is rich, so if there is a need to pay homage at the Caesar's court,
phrases.notes: This refers to representing the Jewish people before the Roman government, which was costly.

phrases.english: he too can go and pay homage.
phrases.notes: Like רבן גמליאל, he can take on this role.

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא עֲשִׂירִי לְעֶזְרָא — דְּאִית לֵיהּ זְכוּת אָבוֹת,
phrases.english: And he is the tenth generation from Ezra, so he has ancestral merit,
phrases.notes: This is exactly what רבי עקיבא lacked.

phrases.english: and he (Rabban Gamliel) will not be able to cause him to be punished.
phrases.notes: This solves the safety concern from step 39.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא חָכָם דְּאִי מַקְשֵׁי לֵיהּ מְפָרֵק לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind each quality listed in step 40.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אלעזר בן עזריה is the right choice.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practical benefit of each of his three qualities.

steps.title: They offer him the position
steps.stepSummary: The Sages approach רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and ask whether he would agree to become head of the ישיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They came and said to him: Would the master agree to be head of the ישיבה?
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves from planning to action. The Sages go to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and formally offer him the leadership.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of simply announcing his appointment, they ask for his consent. This sets up his reply and the consultation that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it agreeable to the master?

phrases.english: They came and said to him:
phrases.notes: The Sages approach the candidate.

phrases.aramaic: נִיחָא לֵיהּ לְמָר דְּלֶיהְוֵי רֵישׁ מְתִיבְתָּא?
phrases.english: Would the master agree to be head of the yeshiva?
phrases.notes: A respectful, formal offer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתוֹ וַאֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ נִיחָא לֵיהּ לְמָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the decision made in steps 40 and 41.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי אלעזר בן עזריה agrees to accept the position.

steps.title: He wants to consult his household first
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה does not answer right away. He says he will first consult with his household.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I will go and consult with my household.
steps.whatsHappening: He replies that he needs to talk it over at home before deciding. His answer is a pause, not a yes or a no.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A role this big affects his whole family, so he does not decide alone. This leads into the conversation with his wife.

keyTerms.meaning: My household, often meaning one's wife

phrases.english: He said to them:
I will go and consult with my household.
phrases.notes: He delays his decision in order to get advice.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ אֵיזִיל וְאִימְּלִיךְ בְּאִינָשֵׁי בֵּיתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replies to the offer in step 42.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He does not decide yet. He will first consult his household.

steps.title: He consults his wife, and she begins to answer
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה goes and consults his wife, and she begins to reply.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and consulted with his wife. She said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: He goes home and asks his wife's advice. This is a setup line: her actual words come on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase אינשי ביתי from the previous step turns out to mean his wife. This passage ends right as she begins to speak, so her advice is the next move in the story.

keyTerms.meaning: His wife (literally, the one of his house)

phrases.english: He went and consulted with his wife.
phrases.notes: Shows that 'my household' meant his wife.

phrases.english: She said to him:
phrases.notes: Her response continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲזַל וְאִמְּלִיךְ בִּדְבֵיתְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the consultation he promised in step 43.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative transition: he seeks his wife's advice, and her reply follows on the next amud.
